method_note: Static pattern analysis over lightly-parsed source. Comments and string literals are blanked before matching, preserving line numbers, so a pattern inside a comment or a revert message never fires. Every finding carries the line that triggered it and states how it produces false positives — the tool narrows what a human reads, it does not replace them.

findings.title: State updated after an external call
findings.explanation: withdraw() makes an external call and then writes contract state. A malicious callee can re-enter before that write lands, so every check made earlier in the function still sees the pre-call state.
findings.false_positives: Not exploitable if the callee is a trusted, fixed address, or if a reentrancy guard modifier already wraps the function — this detector reads the body, not the modifier's implementation.
findings.remediation: Apply checks-effects-interactions: write state before the external call, or add a nonReentrant guard.

findings.title: selfdestruct reachable without an access check
findings.explanation: shutdown() can destroy the contract and there is no owner modifier on it and no msg.sender check in its body. Anyone can call it.
findings.false_positives: A guard implemented through an inherited modifier this detector does not resolve, or an access check delegated to another contract.
findings.remediation: Gate it behind an ownership or role check.

findings.title: Authorization via tx.origin
findings.explanation: tx.origin is the transaction's original sender, not the immediate caller. If this contract is called by another contract the user was tricked into using, tx.origin is still the user and the check passes.
findings.false_positives: Occasionally intentional — a check that the caller is an EOA rather than a contract. That use is itself discouraged and breaks with account abstraction.

findings.title: Randomness derived from block state
findings.explanation: Block timestamp, number, and hash are all influenced or observable by the proposer. A validator can choose whether to publish a block, which is enough to bias any draw derived from them.
findings.false_positives: Fine when the result carries no value — a tiebreak, a display seed, or a nonce that is not security-relevant.
findings.remediation: Use a commit-reveal scheme or a VRF.

findings.title: Privileged state written without an access check
findings.explanation: setFeeRate() is external and assigns to a privileged variable, with no modifier and no msg.sender check in the body.
findings.false_positives: A guard from an inherited modifier this detector does not resolve, or a constructor-like initializer protected by an initialized flag.
findings.remediation: Add an ownership or role modifier.

findings.title: Return value of a low-level call ignored
findings.code: function payout(address payable to, uint256 amount) external {
findings.explanation: call/send/delegatecall return false on failure rather than reverting. Ignoring the result means the transaction continues as if the transfer succeeded.
findings.false_positives: Intentional in fire-and-forget patterns where failure genuinely does not matter, and in some pull-payment designs.
findings.remediation: Check the returned bool, or use a checked wrapper.
